Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

bayesEfron 0.4.0

The defaults of bayes_efron_fit() have changed, so the same data and seed no longer give the posterior draws of 0.3.0. By default, a short preliminary fit (the pilot fit) now chooses the range of the grid, a new Stan program samples the model, and a fit stores the draws of the distribution of effects but no draws for each site. Use settings = "0.3.0" to fit the model as 0.3.0 did, with the same draws if the version of CmdStan and the machine are the same. A fit saved by an earlier version can still be used: its summaries are computed again from its draws with the definitions of this version, and a warning names what was recomputed.

Breaking changes

  • bayes_efron_fit() and make_efron_grid() have a new default grid method, grid_method = "pilot": a pilot fit on the range of 0.3.0 narrows that range to where the distribution of effects lies (see ?make_efron_grid). With this default, make_efron_grid() needs CmdStan. Use grid_method = "paper_realdata" for the range of 0.3.0 without a fit. The first fit of a session that relies on the default says in a message that the defaults have changed.
  • With the default L = NULL, bayes_efron_fit() and make_efron_grid() now choose the number of grid points from the data: 101, or more (up to
    1. when 101 are too few for the smallest standard error or for the spread of the effects. The default was 101 points for every data set. The largest L that can be given is now 401 (was 300).
  • bayes_efron_fit() runs a new Stan program by default. For the same seed its draws differ from the draws of 0.3.0.
  • A fit no longer stores five variables per site (theta_mean, theta_sd, theta_map, theta_rep and log_lik); site_draws = TRUE stores them. The methods of a fit, loo() and waic() included, compute what they need from the draws of the distribution of effects.
  • summary(), confint() and as.data.frame() now compute the limits of a site’s interval as quantiles of the posterior distribution of its effect, which averages over the draws of the distribution of effects. The limits were sample quantiles of the theta_rep draws. Those draws take values on grid points, although R’s interpolation can put their sample quantiles between points. confint(method = "draws") gives those limits for a fit made with site_draws = TRUE.
  • With point masses on the grid, quantiles and tail probabilities are now computed with the probability of each grid point spread evenly over one grid spacing around it (reading = "interpolated"). g_summary(), site_summary(), exceedance_prob() and quantile() have a reading argument, and reading = "step" leaves the probability on the grid point.
  • In the table of site effects, the columns hpdi_lower, hpdi_upper and map are now lower, upper and mode, and the table gains the columns label, estimate and se. confint() returns mean in place of point and, for type = "g", parameter in place of site. The earlier columns remain with the same values and will be removed in 0.5.
  • coef(), confint() and the tables now name the sites by their labels when the data had labels (the sites were numbered before). In the parm argument of confint(), numbers are positions and character strings are labels; parm = "3" was read as the third site. as_bef_data() and bayes_efron_fit() now throw an error for duplicated site labels.
  • The plots use ggplot2, which the package now imports. They carry a caption in place of a title, name the sites by their labels and list them from the top. plot(type = "g") now shows the density of the distribution of effects in place of the probabilities of the grid points, which plot_g(type = "mass") shows.
  • plot(backend = "base") is deprecated and will be removed in 0.5. Until then it plots the four types of 0.3.0 with base graphics and issues a warning once per session. plot() also no longer attaches the plotted numbers to its result (the undocumented attribute bef_plot_payload); g_summary(), site_summary(), exceedance_prob() and diagnose() return them.
  • summary() and plot() now throw an error for an argument that they do not have (it was ignored). plot() still accepts level and sort_by for the four types of 0.3.0.
  • AIC() and BIC() now throw an error that points to loo(). The numbers that they returned were computed from a posterior mean of the log likelihood and are not information criteria.
  • diagnose() now warns about an E-BFMI below 0.3, the value below which CmdStan warns (the threshold was 0.2). An infinite R-hat now fails the check instead of putting R-hat among the diagnostics that could not be computed. A quantity has an infinite R-hat when it stays at one value in each chain and the values differ between chains.
  • bayes_efron_fit() now shows the output of CmdStan and the cmdstanr messages about the sampler in an interactive session only. Use show_messages = TRUE to see them elsewhere.
  • In make_efron_grid(), the arguments after theta_hat and sigma must now be named. The grid method "kl_target_experimental" and the kappa argument are removed, and a grid no longer has a kappa element.
  • A result of summary() that was saved by an earlier version can no longer be printed. Call summary() again on the fit.

New features

  • bayes_efron_fit() has a new settings argument: settings = "0.3.0" runs the Stan program of 0.3.0 with the range, the 101 grid points and the site-level draws of that version. An argument given with it keeps its value. bayes_efron_compile() compiles both Stan programs, and bayes_efron_clear_cache() deletes both compiled models.
  • Three new functions summarize a fit. g_summary() returns the density, the distribution function, quantiles and tail probabilities of the distribution of effects, with intervals. site_summary() returns the table of site effects at any level, and exceedance_prob() the probability that a site effect exceeds a threshold.
  • Ten new functions plot a fit: plot_g(), plot_sites(), plot_shrinkage(), plot_exceedance(), plot_site_posterior(), plot_diagnostics(), plot_loo(), plot_ppc(), plot_recovery() and plot_mcmc(). They return ggplot objects, except that plot_mcmc(type = "pairs") returns a grid of plots. plot() of a fit calls them through type, where "sites" and "diagnostics" replace "caterpillar" and "diagnostic"; the earlier names are still accepted.
  • bayes_efron_fit(), make_efron_grid() and compare_efron_grids() accept a data frame or a bef_data object as their first argument.
  • as_bef_data() takes the labels of a metafor escalc object from its slab, and its result has an as.data.frame() method. For a data frame with variances and no standard errors it takes the square roots, with a message. It warns when a column with a name that begins with vi or var is given as the standard errors.
  • bayes_efron_fit() and make_efron_grid() have a new margin argument for the "pilot" method, which sets how far the region found by the pilot fit is extended on each side, as a fraction of its width. make_efron_grid() also has a seed argument for the pilot fit.
  • bayes_efron_fit() and make_efron_grid() gain a support argument, which gives the two limits of the grid directly, and a knots argument, for which "grid" is the only value so far. bayes_efron_fit() also takes a grid made by make_efron_grid() as grid. A grid has the class bef_grid, with print() and plot() methods.
  • component = "normal" puts a normal distribution with a standard deviation of width grid spacings at each grid point, in place of a point mass, as in the penalized Gaussian mixture of Sui and Tipton (2026).
  • A warning of class bef_warn_grid_resolution reports a grid that is too coarse for the smallest standard error or for the spread of the effects, or narrower than the median standard error.
  • diagnose() reports, for each end of the grid, the largest posterior probability that a site has in the outer 2% of the range, and the posterior distribution of the standard deviation of the effects together with its prior. bayes_efron_fit() issues a warning of class bef_warn_grid_ends when that probability exceeds 0.05 at an end that was specified in support or that follows from the estimates alone. The result of diagnose() has an as.data.frame() method.
  • confint() has the new arguments method and interval, with interval = "hpd" for the shortest interval, and its result prints the level and the kind of interval.
  • A fit has the new methods quantile(), simulate() for joint draws of the site effects, residuals(), posterior::ndraws() and posterior::variables(). vcov(full = TRUE) returns the covariances between the site effects, and coef(type = "mode") is the new name of type = "map", which is still accepted.
  • print() of a fit shows the number of draws, the range of the standard errors, the grid with the method that chose its range, and the functions to call next.
  • predict() accepts a data frame of estimates and standard errors as newdata. It then returns the posterior summaries of new sites with known estimates, with intervals at level: for each row, the summaries that the site would have in a fit of the data with that site added.
  • bayes_efron_fit() gains the sampler arguments refresh, init, thin and show_messages. thin reduces what is stored; the sampler diagnostics still describe the whole run.
  • compare_efron_grids() accepts several grid methods, ranges given in support and both kinds of component, and keep_fits = TRUE returns the fits as well. For each specification it also returns the range, the mean and the standard deviation of the distribution of effects, the posterior means of the sites named in sites, the posterior probability at the ends of the grid (as in diagnose()), and whether the grid is fine enough. It reports which fit is running, and its result has a plot() method. A comparison saved by 0.3.0 cannot be plotted and has to be run again.
  • New as_normalmix() returns the posterior mean of the distribution of effects as a normalmix object, which the ebnm package accepts as a fixed prior. With the bayesplot package installed, nuts_params(), log_posterior(), rhat() and neff_ratio() work on a fit. Both packages are suggested: bayesplot for the plots of the sampler, and ebnm for the comparison with empirical Bayes methods.
  • krw_discrimination and twin_towers are new data sets. krw_discrimination contains the firm-level callback gaps of Kline, Rose and Walters, from the public replication files of Walters (2024), as analyzed by Lee and Sui (2025). Both data sets record where they come from in the attribute source, and the scripts that rebuild them from the public files are in data-raw/ in the source repository.
  • star_schools is a new data set from a multisite trial in education: the estimated effect of small classes in each of the 79 kindergarten schools of Tennessee’s Project STAR. The estimates are built from the public student file with a model that has a random intercept for each class. The data set also has the estimates and standard errors that take the students of a school as independent.
  • The stored fits krw_fit and twin_towers_fit are new. Like raudenbush_fit, they are made with the grid method, the Stan program and the storage of this version (twin_towers_fit with 8 spline functions) and are thinned to 800 of 12,000 draws (thin = 15), so that the examples run without CmdStan. raudenbush_fit has the range that it had in 0.3.0 but different draws.

Bug fixes

  • predict(type = "theta_hat") with several standard errors now gives each new site an effect of its own, drawn from the same posterior draw of the distribution of effects. All the new sites of a draw had the same true effect, so that their estimates differed by sampling error alone.
  • compare_efron_grids() no longer fails with an internal error when one of its fits fails. It issues a warning that names the specification and returns a row of missing values for it, as documented.
  • The errors of bayes_efron_fit() and compare_efron_grids() about the data now state in one sentence what is wrong: a missing value, an infinite value, a length or a sign. A missing value was reported inside a sentence about the type and the length of the vector.
  • make_efron_grid(grid = ) no longer throws an error about grid_method, the argument that the name was matched to. Its error now points to support and L, and compare_efron_grids(grid = ) reports that a grid cannot be given.
  • In the posterior standard deviation of a site, the variance between draws is now divided by the number of draws, as its definition requires (was the number of draws minus one).

Documentation

  • The help pages and the vignettes are rewritten in plainer language. All ten vignettes are built around the data sets and stored fits listed above, with the callback gaps (krw_discrimination) as the main example. Four are new: twin-towers, on the recovery of a distribution with two groups; empirical-bayes, a comparison with the ebnm and deconvolveR packages; plots, a gallery of the plot functions; and teacher-expectancy, which keeps the 19 studies that were the main example of 0.3.0 as a second case, with a simulation of what the model can and cannot do with so few.
  • The article “Small classes in 79 schools” on the package website analyzes star_schools: how the effect varies across schools according to the fit, how much of that rests on the standard errors, and what simulated data sets with known effects show. The article and the fit that it uses are not installed with the package.
  • The installed files benchmark-coverage.csv and benchmark-remedies.csv (in verification/) and grid_comparison_example.rds (in examples/) are replaced by the tables and the stored comparisons that the vignettes of this version use.

bayesEfron 0.3.0

This is the first public release since 0.1.0. It includes the changes of 0.2.0, which was not released separately and is described below. The model is the same as in 0.2.0: with the same data, settings, seed and version of CmdStan on the same machine, the posterior draws are identical.

Breaking changes

  • In the table of site effects that summary() and as.data.frame() return, sd is now the posterior standard deviation of each effect and map its posterior mode, as defined in Lee and Sui (2025, Section 4.3 and Appendix A). Earlier versions gave the standard deviation and the mode for a given distribution of effects, averaged over the posterior draws of that distribution. That sd left out the uncertainty about the distribution (the posterior standard deviations of the example data are 3% to 35% larger), and that map was not, in general, the mode of the posterior distribution. vcov() and coef(type = "map") change with them. The posterior means and the intervals are unchanged.
  • A fit saved by an earlier version holds sd and map in the earlier definitions, and one saved by 0.1.0 holds effective_params in its first definition too. summary(), coef(), vcov() and the other methods of a fit compute these again from the stored draws and give a warning that names what changed; the saved object is not altered. A saved result of summary() cannot be brought up to date and has to be made again from the fit. A fit saved by 0.1.0 still has to be fitted again before diagnose(), loo(), waic() or predict() can be used.
  • The compiled model is now handled by cmdstanr alone. It is stored in tools::R_user_dir("bayesEfron", "cache") under a name made of a hash of the Stan file, the CmdStan version and the machine architecture, and is recompiled when one of them changes. The lock files and the files with metadata that earlier versions wrote next to it are gone. The environment variable BAYESEFRON_CACHE_ROOT still moves the directory.
  • bayes_efron_clear_cache() deletes the compiled models and returns their number. The values "session", "compiled_models" and "lock_only" of its argument scope are accepted with a warning and will be removed; "lock_only" no longer does anything. Files left by earlier versions are deleted as well.
  • bayes_efron_compile() no longer has the argument seed_for_check.
  • plot() no longer has type = "sensitivity", which drew the same picture as type = "caterpillar".
  • Three environment variables are replaced. Use plot(backend = "base") for BAYESEFRON_NO_GGPLOT2, options(bayesEfron.use_cli = FALSE) for BAYESEFRON_NO_CLI, and the argument parallel_chains of bayes_efron_fit() for BAYESEFRON_PARALLEL_CHAINS.
  • The environment variables that switched parts of the test suite on (BAYESEFRON_RUN_LIVE, BAYESEFRON_RUN_FULL_LIVE, BAYESEFRON_RUN_PARITY, BAYESEFRON_TIER3_OK_TO_REFIT, BAYESEFRON_TIER3_FULL_LIVE_MATRIX, BAYESEFRON_SOURCE_ROOT and BAYESEFRON_ENFORCE_RELEASE_LEDGER) are no longer read. The tests that fit a model run when CmdStan is installed and are skipped when it is not.
  • Condition classes that were never signaled are removed, as are the elements stage, module and predicate of error objects. The class bayesEfron_validate_error is now bef_validate_error. Every error of the package still inherits from bef_error.
  • The element attribution of the list that make_efron_grid() returns names the section of Lee and Sui (2025) that a rule comes from.
  • The packages ps, jsonlite, deconvolveR and desc are no longer suggested.

New features

  • bayes_efron_fit() has the arguments max_treedepth and parallel_chains.
  • A fit records the settings of the sampler and the versions of bayesEfron and cmdstanr that made it, as attributes of metadata (see ?bef_fit).
  • plot() has the argument backend, "ggplot2" or "base".
  • The data set raudenbush1985, 19 studies of teacher expectancy, and raudenbush_fit, the model fitted to it with the default settings. All examples and vignettes use them and run without CmdStan.
  • ?bef_fit describes the fitted object and lists its methods.
  • A compiled model that does not run is detected and compiled again (on Windows only an empty file is detected).

Bug fixes

  • predict(type = "theta_hat", n = 1) stopped with an error when several standard errors were given. It returns a matrix with one row.
  • The variance of an effect given the distribution of effects, from which sd and effective_params are computed, was taken as a difference of two moments. That loses its digits when the estimates are very far from zero compared with their standard errors. The variance is now taken about the mean. Results for estimates of ordinary size are unchanged.
  • loo() returned NaN as the Monte Carlo standard error of a site whose likelihood was so small that it rounded to zero.
  • A fit with fewer than 400 draws was not checked at all. It is now checked for divergent transitions, iterations at the maximum tree depth and E-BFMI. R-hat and the effective sample sizes are still not compared with their thresholds in such a fit, and diagnostic_skipped says so.
  • A fit in which R-hat or an effective sample size was infinite for some quantity stopped with an error. The diagnostic is now stored as NA and named in diagnostic_skipped.
  • iter_sampling = 0 was accepted, and the function stopped with an error only after the warmup had run. It is now rejected with the other arguments.
  • compare_efron_grids() put elpd_diff and se_diff in the wrong rows with loo 2.10 or later, so that the best specification could show the largest difference. They are now computed from the pointwise values.
  • bayes_efron_fit() called set.seed(), which reset R’s random number generator for the rest of the session and made two fits with the same seed write to the same temporary files. It no longer does.
  • plot(type = "g") drew the summaries of the distribution, not the distribution, for a fit made with the default settings. It now computes the probabilities from the draws.
  • plot(type = "diagnostic") with ggplot2 drew five diagnostics of different scales on one axis. Each has its own panel.
  • print() and summary() showed the names of the same diagnostics under three labels. There are now two, failed checks and warnings.
  • Errors named an internal helper as their source. They name the function that was called.
  • fitted() stopped when given further arguments; it ignores them, as the other methods do.
  • predict(seed = ) left R’s random number generator seeded when the session had not used it before. It now leaves the generator as it found it.
  • plot(type = "loo", backend = "base") drew the reference lines at 0.5 and 0.7 only when the values reached them. Both backends now show them always.
  • print() and summary() showed the number of iterations at the maximum tree depth under the label max treedepth, which read as a depth. The label is now treedepth hits. The titles and axis labels of the plots say what is drawn (“Distribution of effects” and so on).
  • The stored test inputs held the local paths of the files they were made from.

Documentation

  • The help pages are rewritten. They say what the columns of the table of site effects are. In particular hpdi_lower and hpdi_upper are the 5% and 95% quantiles of the posterior draws and not the limits of a highest posterior density interval.
  • The README says how to install the vignettes with the package; an installation from GitHub does not build them unless asked to.
  • Six vignettes replace sixteen: bayesEfron, data-input, choosing-a-grid, diagnostics, model and implementation.
  • vignette("choosing-a-grid") shows how far the results for the example data depend on the grid. With 19 studies the posterior mean of the study with the largest estimate changes with the width of the grid and the number of spline functions, while the summaries of the distribution of effects and the other studies hardly change.
  • The table of coverage on the benchmark of Lee and Sui (2025) reports, for each number of sites, how many fits did not converge. With 1,500 sites and the default settings three of twenty did not, and a second table shows what a narrower grid and a larger maximum tree depth change for those three. The scripts and the data of the benchmark are in data-raw/benchmark/ in the source repository.

bayesEfron 0.2.0

Not released separately.

Breaking changes

  • effective_params is the sum over sites of the posterior variance of the effect, for a given distribution of effects, divided by the squared standard error. Version 0.1.0 reported the number of sites minus that sum.
  • fit$posterior holds only the draws of mean_g, var_g, sd_g, effective_params and log_marginal_likelihood. The draws for each site are in fit$draws, and fit$metadata$theta_rep_draws is removed.
  • The draws no longer include g and log_w; store_grid_quantities = TRUE puts them back.
  • diagnose() returns R-hat and the effective sample sizes for every quantity in the draws, where 0.1.0 returned one number for all of them together, and it returns E-BFMI. R-hat above 1.05 or a divergent transition is a failed check; R-hat above 1.01, an effective sample size below 400, an iteration at the maximum tree depth and E-BFMI below 0.2 are warnings.
  • Objects saved by 0.1.0 can still be used with summary(), coef(), confint(), as.data.frame(), nobs() and print(). diagnose(), loo(), waic() and predict() need the model to be fitted again.

New features

  • loo() and waic() methods, and plot(type = "loo").
  • compare_efron_grids() fits several specifications of the grid and of the spline basis and ranks them by leave-one-out cross-validation.
  • predict() draws the effect or the estimate of a new site, and fitted() returns the posterior means.
  • as_bef_data() accepts a data frame, finds the columns by name and takes variances as well as standard errors. It stops on missing values.

Performance

  • The sampler is about 12 to 34 times faster than in 0.1.0 for 200 to 1,500 sites, and a fitted object is about half the size. The normal densities of the estimates at the grid points are computed once, and the likelihood is one matrix product.

bayesEfron 0.1.0

First public release.

  • bayes_efron_fit() fits the fully Bayesian Efron log-spline model to estimates and their standard errors.
  • make_efron_grid() builds the grid and the spline basis, with three rules from Lee and Sui (2025) and one experimental rule.
  • as_bef_data() converts a list or a metafor::escalc() object.
  • bayes_efron_compile() and bayes_efron_clear_cache() manage the compiled model.
  • Methods for fitted objects: summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), as.data.frame(), nobs(), logLik(), posterior::as_draws(), diagnose() and plot().
